title: phUSD and rewardToken are not `immutable`: the un-keyed banks' safety rests on absence-of-setter, not the compiler
description: The NatSpec at :168-171 justifies the un-token-keyed phUSD bank with 'phUSD is fixed at construction and never rotates'. That is true today -- both phUSD (:51) and rewardToken (:54) are constructor-only (assigned :243-244) with zero-address validation and no setter exists (verified by grep; the `immutable` keyword appears NOWHERE in the file) -- but they are PLAIN STORAGE, not `immutable`. The safety of both un-keyed banks (unclaimablePhUSDOf, unclaimableStableOf) rests on the continued ABSENCE OF A SETTER rather than on a compiler guarantee. A future setter would silently strand every banked balance under the old asset. The design is internally consistent: promoToken DOES rotate (:403 / :559), which is exactly why unclaimablePromoOf is token-keyed.
impact: None today. Hardening / future-proofing of the un-keyed banks' keying invariant.
recommendation: Declare phUSD and rewardToken `immutable` so the banks' keying invariant is enforced by the compiler rather than by convention. Zero runtime cost; also saves an SLOAD per claim.
corroboration: Independently corroborated by 4naly3er GAS-10 ('State variables only set in the constructor should be declared immutable'), which flags PhlimboV3.sol:244.
severityRationale: QA. No value at risk today; the invariant currently holds.
